PullRequest.Title: sessions: add experimental Compare Models spotlight
PullRequest.Body: Fixes #345917 Adds `sessions.chat.compareAgents.showSpotlight`, an experimental application setting that defaults to `false`. When enabled, opening an eligible model picker shows a one-time spotlight on Compare Models. The callout explains running the same prompt across models and agent harnesses, with an optional judge and synthesizer where available. Workspace-less chats receive comparison-only guidance. - Reuses onboarding eligibility, shown-state persistence, the accessible spotlight dialog, Escape dismissal, and focus restoration. - Honors disabled AI and onboarding, avoids interrupting another onboarding presentation, and cancels pending guidance when the picker closes. - Keeps comparison-specific behavior in Sessions. A small disposable render hook exposes the owned toggle without querying another component’s DOM. - Updates the existing accessibility help. Does not change comparison execution or runtime permissions. ### How to test 1. In the Agents window, enable `sessions.chat.compareAgents.showSpotlight` and leave `onboarding.enabled` enabled. 2. Open an eligible new-session model picker. Verify the Compare Models icon is spotlighted and the callout explains parallel models/harnesses and optional judging/synthesis. 3. Activate Understood or press Escape. Verify focus returns to the picker and it remains usable. Reopen it and verify the introduction does not repeat. 4. Reset this scenario with the onboarding developer reset command to retry. Activate the highlighted Compare Models control and verify setup opens without sending a prompt. 5. Verify the setting off, disabled AI/onboarding, and an unavailable comparison do not show guidance. In a workspace-less chat, verify it does not advertise judging/synthesis. ### Validation - `pnpm run compile-client` — passed, including client type checking. - `corepack pnpm run valid-layers-check` — passed. - Changed-TypeScript ESLint — passed for all 12 changed files. - The following browser command — passed, 478 tests, including actual spotlight rendering, accessible description, Escape/Understood focus restoration, toggle lifecycle, and existing picker/composer behavior: ```sh corepack pnpm run test-browser-no-install --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/compareAgentsSpotlight.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/sessionComparisonModelSelection.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/sessionsChatAccessibilityHelp.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/newChatWidget.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/input/modelPicker/modelPickerTabbedWidget.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/actionWidget/test/browser/tabbedActionListWidget.test.ts --browser chromium --reporter dot ``` Live-provider/manual workbench flows and full integration/smoke suites were not run.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The register/dispose event fan-out and synchronous picker call path are directly traced in repository code. The only magnitude uncertainty is the current number of scenarios/listeners and whether Settings UI is open; repetition after dismissal is deterministic because shown state and comparison-discovered state are separate.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Synchronous CPU work, configuration-schema/default rebuilding, observable trigger subscriptions, and global registry events
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each eligible model-picker open performs one global scenario registration and popup disposal performs one deregistration; every mutation rescans all registered onboarding scenarios/descriptors and rebuilds their trigger/configuration state, so cost grows with picker-open frequency and global onboarding scenario count.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased model-picker open/close latency and avoidable main-thread CPU work
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Opening or closing the model picker did not mutate the global onboarding registry or configuration registry.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Rendering the Compare Models toggle registers a short-lived global onboarding scenario; closing or rerendering the popup disposes it. This still happens after the one-time scenario has been shown because the constructor only checks the feature setting and current registry membership, while the separate discovered flag is written only when comparison setup starts.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 66 registers the scenario into the global registry for the rendered button lifetime; the same new object's disposal unregisters it. No equivalent registry mutation existed on picker rendering before this diff.
Findings.Title: Skip global scenario registration once the spotlight is shown
Findings.Impact: With the setting enabled, a user who dismisses the introduction with Understood/Escape but does not open comparison setup pays two global registry updates on every later model-picker open. Each update synchronously rebuilds onboarding trigger listeners/evaluation and the developer-mode configuration node, which emits configuration/schema updates on the picker UI path.
Findings.Evidence: `onboardingScenarioRegistry.register` fires `onDidChange` synchronously, and its returned disposable fires it again. The onboarding service listener calls `_registerTriggerListeners`, `_resolveExperiments`, and `_evaluate`; the onboarding contribution rebuilds/sorts all scenario descriptors and calls `configurationRegistry.updateConfigurations`, which emits schema/default configuration updates; the tryout service also clears and reconstructs its contribution listeners. `shouldShowNudge` later suppresses presentation but is only checked after this registration fan-out, and `SessionComparisonModelSelection.start()` is the only path that sets the separate discovered storage key.
Findings.Recommendation: Before registering, short-circuit on `onboardingService.hasBeenShown(COMPARE_AGENTS_SPOTLIGHT_ID)` (while preserving developer-mode semantics if needed), or keep one stable scenario registration and vary only the per-button target. This retains retries before the spotlight is actually shown without rebuilding global onboarding/configuration state on every later picker open.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open an eligible model picker for the first time with the experimental spotlight enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Popup rendering synchronously constructs CompareAgentsSpotlight, marks the button, registers the scenario, and triggers all global registry listeners before the popup render returns. Overlay creation is deferred to the next animation frame; onboarding presentation then serializes through the global presentation queue.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist onboarding shown state and outcome through Memento/IStorageService
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two bounded saves for one displayed spotlight: one when presentation starts and one when it ends.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Opening this picker did not run an onboarding scenario or persist its shown/outcome state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The shown-state save occurs before presentation rendering; outcome persistence occurs after dismissal. Neither scales with models.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Emit onboarding shown and outcome telemetry through configured appenders
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most two bounded telemetry events for the one-time displayed spotlight.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No Compare Models spotlight telemetry was emitted.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The shown event runs after visible presentation callback and the outcome event after dismissal; no per-model fan-out.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One Compare Models toggle per picker render; global work scales with the total registered onboarding scenarios/descriptors and observable triggers, not model count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All registration/configuration work is serialized on the UI thread. The onboarding service globally queues presentations and coalesces duplicate runs by scenario id.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Configuration, registry, entitlement, and shown state are warm in memory. A cold eligible first display writes shown state; no result cache avoids the initial registration. The comparison-discovered storage flag suppresses later construction only after comparison setup is opened.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: constructor-to-render path, synchronous registry events, deferred frame, queueing, and bounded persistence/telemetry are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact synchronous registry/configuration duration depends on the number of registered scenarios and listeners in the running product.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable repeated global registry/configuration work is introduced on this path; the one-time overlay DOM, storage, and telemetry work is bounded.

Scenarios.Scenario: Reopen the model picker after dismissing the one-time spotlight without starting comparison setup
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Popup rendering again registers the already-shown scenario, synchronously rebuilding onboarding trigger listeners, experiment evaluation, developer-mode configuration/schema state, and tryout listeners; disposal on popup close repeats the same fan-out. shouldShowNudge suppresses only the later presentation.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Two global registry mutations per picker open/close, multiplied by repeated picker use and by all onboarding scenarios/descriptors.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous and serialized on the UI thread; no limiter or coalescing exists for registry/configuration rebuilds.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm persisted shown state prevents the overlay run, but it is consulted only after registration. The positive comparison-discovered state is still false unless the user starts comparison, so it does not cache this negative path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: shown state and comparison-discovered state are separate, and all registry listeners are directly visible in code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Per-open milliseconds vary with registry size and active Settings/configuration listeners, but the repeated work and critical-path placement are deterministic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported: avoid registration after persisted shown state makes the scenario ineligible.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open comparison setup from the highlighted toggle or close the picker while guidance is pending
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Starting comparison persists the existing discovered flag, rerenders the picker, and disposes the render-owned spotlight, canceling its frame or queued/running scenario. Closing also disposes the render store and cancellation source.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the comparison-discovered flag through IStorageService
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One write when comparison setup is first or subsequently opened.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same discovered flag was persisted when comparison setup started.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The synchronous store call precedes draft-state update, but this operation already existed before the diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One cancellation/disposal chain per picker lifetime; independent of model count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: UI actions are serialized; onboarding cancellation removes a queued entry or aborts the single active presentation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The discovered flag is persisted application-wide and future renderToggle calls return Disposable.None. Pending scheduled-frame work is canceled by disposal.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: render disposable ownership and cancellation paths are explicit and tested.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Storage backend latency is environment-dependent, but the diff does not increase this boundary cardinality.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional performance issue: scheduled work and registrations are disposed, and the persisted positive state suppresses future construction.

Scenarios.Scenario: Show any onboarding spotlight after the shared SpotlightOverlay change
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each step assigns an id only if the target lacks one, writes a flow-to dataset entry, installs the existing resize/scroll/animation listeners, and performs layout.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One UUID assignment at most per target element and one constant-time flow-to write per shown step.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Animation/layout scheduling remains coalesced to animation frames; one active spotlight presentation is globally serialized.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The generated target id remains on the element and is reused on later steps; no collection or cache grows.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added operations are direct DOM/string work and existing listener cleanup remains in the per-step store.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: UUID generation cost is trivial relative to existing spotlight layout work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: added work is bounded and does not add layout reads, boundary calls, or retained collections.

Scenarios.Scenario: Move focus between a tabbed action-list popup and a logically flow-linked spotlight callout
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The popup blur callback traverses DOM parents and at most one id-based flow-to link before deciding whether to hide.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One traversal per blur, bounded by shallow DOM ancestry rather than models or list rows.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous browser focus handling on the UI thread; no asynchronous or concurrent work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved; the flow-to link is a dataset id lookup.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: `isAncestorUsingFlowTo` is a simple parent walk with `getElementById` only on marked nodes.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: DOM depth varies, but realistic picker/callout trees are shallow and the event is not frame-frequency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the additional focus traversal is bounded and necessary to prevent popup teardown during the spotlight.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the model picker with the new spotlight setting disabled (default) or after comparison discovery
Scenarios.CriticalPath: renderToggle either constructs a small object that returns after one configuration read, or returns Disposable.None before instantiation when discovered.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One constant-time check per picker render.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous UI-thread check; no queued work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Configuration and discovered storage values are memory-backed observables; discovered positive state avoids construction entirely.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both early-return branches are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression on the default-disabled path.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 14 changed files. One medium-confidence/high-evidence repeated-work regression was submitted: short-lived scenario registration causes global onboarding and configuration/schema rebuilds on every post-dismiss picker open. Other UI, lifecycle, persistence, telemetry, and focus-flow changes are bounded or properly disposed.
